items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: Buster Williams and I go back to the ‘70s... we kind of — we met each other you know — I never got a chance to really collaborate with him

ctx.x: So I have a couple of observations. You had a sort of a lengthy bass intro to the tune, and two people came to mind while you were playing. One was Henry Grimes and the other is Buster Williams.

Yeah. Two of my guys, yeah, two of my guys. Buster Williams and I go back to the ‘70s you know when he was playing with Herbie and Mwandishi. And those guys used to come to Buffalo. And we kind of — we met each other you know — I never got a chance to really collaborate with him but I always admired, he’s a great bass player. Henry Grimes I actually got a chance to play with. He came to Buffalo a couple of years before he passed, and he came to the club and he was playing — you know he played violin too —
